prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. System: Regional Flow Platform alias Cedarbell (coordination only; shares regional context each cycle). Parts: Demand Prediction Service alias Marlinstone (refreshes stand demand on material off-block change); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM); Slot Allocation Engine alias Blueharbor (matches Marlinstone demand to CAM constraints; inputs Flight Intent Message, Airport Capacity Plan, Airport Acceptance Rate, runway metering limits, sector loading; in Ground Delay Program derives Calculated Takeoff Time/arrival opportunity within capacity envelope before local preference; priority: safety-critical/emergency/humanitarian/national, then scheduled per Business Rules Registry fairness, then GA/discretionary; shall not excessively delay one operator for another unless rule basis visible+logged; operator preferences advisory; Target Off Block Time tests readiness, unready aircraft resequenced); Airport CDM Portal alias Foxglove (publishes results; duty confirmations); Digital Briefing Room; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board (movement updates→Audit Event Ledger); Departure Metering Service; Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console; Weather Ingest Gateway alias Orchard; Flight Data Exchange; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Airline Interface Adapter (supplies operator preferences); Alert Distribution Hub; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Audit Event Ledger; Identity Access Service; Business Rules Registry; Time Synchronization Service; Collaborative Decision Log (records material resequencing: reason, aircraft, parties, approval time); East/West Apron Sensors; runway meters; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner; Common Situation Display. Actors: Regional Flow Manager alias Copperfin (owns priority policy; authorizes temporary rule changes in Capacity Reduction State); Airline Operations Coordinator alias Saffron (Flight Intent Message, Target Off Block Time); Aircraft Operator Representative; Slot Coordinator (administers allocation run, reviews exceptions, confirms publication readiness; Calculated Takeoff Time); Airport Duty Manager (Airport Capacity Plan; Runway Inspection Note); Tower Supervisor alias Brindle; Ramp Control Lead alias Quartzline (Stand Tow Request Form; escalates to Brindle+Duty Manager); Ground Handling Dispatcher; Meteorology Briefing Officer (Storm Cell Snapshot); Data Governance Steward; System Support Engineer. Flows: Flight Intent Message→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange→Marlinstone; Orchard→CAM;

New part:
S237: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the delay slip when requesting an exemption review for a crew connectivity constraint that is not already represented in the allocation data.
S238: Exemption requests are evaluated against safety impact, network impact, passenger impact, crew legality, and the availability of a lower-impact alternative.
S239: The Slot Coordinator records each accepted or rejected exemption in the Collaborative Decision Log with the rule applied, the approving role, and the expected operational consequence.
S240: The Data Governance Steward ensures that exemption categories, priority codes, and fairness metrics are versioned in the Business Rules Registry before they are used in live allocation.
S241: The Arrival Regulation Console presents proposed arrival opportunities with the capacity source, regulation start time, and expected delay for each affected flight.
S242: The Departure Metering Service presents proposed departure opportunities and associated Calculated Takeoff Time values for coordination with the Tower Sequence Manager.
S243: The Tower Supervisor may reject a proposed departure opportunity when runway safety, wake spacing, or local sequencing conditions make the proposal impracticable.
S244: The Ramp Control Lead may identify apron constraints through the Ramp Movement Board, but the Slot Allocation Engine remains responsible for recalculating the regulated opportunity.
S245: All allocation runs are time stamped by the Time Synchronization Service and written to the Audit Event Ledger for later reconstruction of the decision sequence.
S246: During Normal Operations, allocation results are refreshed at regular intervals, while Adverse Weather Mode and Recovery Phase allow shorter recalculation cycles approved by the Regional Flow Manager.
S247: If the Regional Flow Platform enters Contingency Fallback State, the Contingency Operations Console preserves the last valid allocation, supports manual amendments, and marks the resulting Slot Compliance State as provisional.
S248: Post-event assessment in the Performance Analytics Warehouse compares proposed opportunities, actual movement times, exemption usage, and operator-level delay equity to improve subsequent rule calibration.
S249: Collaborative target time management establishes a shared operating baseline for each departure by linking the Target Off Block Time, the Calculated Takeoff Time, and the key surface milestone timestamps to the same flight record.
S250: The Regional Flow Platform creates the initial Target Off Block Time proposal from current flight intent, stand readiness, turnaround progress, and applicable airport capacity constraints.
S251: The Demand Prediction Service estimates demand pressure over the next planning horizon and marks flights whose proposed Target Off Block Time values are likely to cause runway or sector imbalance.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
